::: {.lead}
Today you plan a small digital service and build its order form. Each
experiment has two parts. **Part A** is in Microsoft Forms and Word (your
university account). **Part B** is on a simulator of the interactive
lesson: on paper, scan its QR code; on the screen, click its link. After
each step, write your result in its box. At the end, copy your key results
into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a lab computer with a browser (Microsoft Forms at
  `forms.office.com`, with your university account) and Word. Google Forms
  works in the same way.
- **No lab computer today?** Do Part B of each experiment on your phone.
  Microsoft Forms also works in the browser of a phone.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

{{< start-files >}}

## Experiment 1 · Kinds of digital services

**The idea:** a **digital service** is a service that customers use on the
Internet. Four common kinds: an **online store** (choose products and pay),
a **booking** (choose a day and a time), an **online form** (answer
questions, such as an order or a survey) and a **digital product** (a file
that you download, such as an e-book).

**Aim:** tell the kinds of digital services apart.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (a browser)**
:::

1. Open `forms.office.com` and sign in. Look at the ready-made forms
   (templates) at the top: for example a registration, a feedback or an
   order form.

   {{< record "The name of one template" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   For example **Event registration** or **Customer feedback**. A template
   is a ready-made form: you change only the questions.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   An event registration form: people choose a day and a place. Which kind
   of service is it close to?

   - [x] a booking

     Why: People reserve a place on a day.

   - [ ] a digital product

     Why: Nobody downloads a file.

   - [ ] an online store

     Why: Nobody chooses products to pay for.
   :::

2. On your phone or the computer, think of the university e-learning
   platform: you open a page, do the tasks and upload a file.

   {{< record "Is the e-learning platform a digital service: yes or no?" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Yes**: students use it on the Internet, from any phone or computer.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Is the e-learning platform of the university a digital service?

   - [x] yes

     Why: Students use it on the Internet, from any device.

   - [ ] no, it is only a website

     Why: A site where people do things (tasks, uploads) is a service.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/service-sorter.html" poster="sims/service-sorter.png" title="Service Sorter: which kind of digital service?" >}}

3. In **Service Sorter**, sort the eight services. Which kind is "Fix It:
   choose a day and a time to repair your phone"?

   {{< record "Fix It is" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **A booking**: the customer chooses a day and a time.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which kind of digital service? Sort them.

   online store
   :   Choose notebooks, pay, get them at home.

       Why: Products and an online payment.

   booking
   :   Book the library study room for one hour.

       Why: A room for a time.

   online form
   :   The canteen survey of ten questions.

       Why: Questions that people answer.

   digital product
   :   An e-book that you download.

       Why: The product is a file.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · A plan: the customer, the need, the steps

**The idea:** before you build a service, write a short **plan**: **who**
the customer is, **what** the customer needs, and the **steps** that the
customer takes, in order. Then you know what to build.

**Aim:** plan a small service in three parts.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. Open `service-plan-start.docx`. Mona makes cakes at home and wants to
   take orders online. After each line, type the right words from this
   list: *an online form* · *families who want a cake for a party* · *to
   order a cake without a phone call*.

   {{< record "The customer: … ; the need: …" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Kind: **an online form**. Customer: **families who want a cake for a
   party**. Need: **to order a cake without a phone call**.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Who is the customer of Mona's order service?

   - [x] families who want a cake for a party

     Why: The customer is the person who uses the service.

   - [ ] Mona

     Why: Mona gives the service; she is not its customer.

   - [ ] the bank

     Why: The bank does not order cakes.
   :::

2. Under *The steps of the customer*, type the four steps in order: *See
   the cakes and their prices* · *Fill in the order form* · *Get a
   confirmation* · *Collect the cake and pay*. Save the file.

   {{< record "Step 2 is" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Fill in the order form**: first the customer sees the cakes, then
   orders, then gets a confirmation, then collects and pays.
   :::

   ::: {.order}
   Put the steps of the customer in order.

   1. See the cakes and their prices
   2. Fill in the order form
   3. Get a confirmation
   4. Collect the cake and pay

   Why: The customer chooses first, then orders, gets a confirmation, and collects.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/service-planner.html" poster="sims/service-planner.png" title="Service Planner: the customer, the need, the steps" >}}

3. In **Service Planner**, plan Mona's service: the customer, the need and
   the order of the steps.

   {{< record "Which part of the service do you build next?" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **The order form**: step 2 of the customer.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   The plan is ready. Which part do you build next?

   - [x] the order form

     Why: The customer orders with the form: step 2 of the plan.

   - [ ] a new oven

     Why: The plan is about the online service.

   - [ ] a printed menu

     Why: The customers see the cakes online.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · An order form linked to a spreadsheet

**The idea:** an **online form** (Microsoft Forms, Google Forms) is a page
of questions. Each question has a **type**: **Choice** (tap an option),
**Text**, **Number** or **Date**. Every **response** (one filled-in form)
becomes **one row** of a spreadsheet: Responses › **Open results in
Excel**.

**Aim:** build a short order form, send one test order, and find it in the
sheet.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Microsoft Forms)**
:::

1. In Microsoft Forms, click **New Form**. Title: `Mona's Cakes: order`.
   Add three questions: **Choice** *Which cake?* (Chocolate, Lemon, Fruit),
   **Text** *How many cakes?* (Restrictions: Number), **Date** *Pick-up
   day*.

   {{< record "The type of Which cake?" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Choice**: the customer taps one of the three cakes, so every answer is
   written the same way.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which question type? Sort the questions.

   Choice
   :   Which cake? (Chocolate, Lemon, Fruit)

       Why: The customer taps one of the options.

   Number
   :   How many cakes?

       Why: A number that Mona can add up.

   Date
   :   Pick-up day

       Why: A day in the calendar.
   :::

2. Click **Preview**, fill in one test order and **Submit**. Then click
   **Responses › Open results in Excel**.

   {{< record "My test order is in row" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Row 2**: row 1 has the questions, and every response is one new row.
   :::

   ::: {.fill answer="2|row 2" hint="Row 1 has the names of the questions."}
   The sheet of the responses has the questions in row 1. In which row is
   the first order?

   Why: Every response is one new row under the questions: the first one is in row 2.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/form-builder.html" poster="sims/form-builder.png" title="Form Builder: an order form and its sheet" >}}

3. In **Form Builder**, give the four questions their types, then send a
   test order. What happens in the sheet?

   {{< record "The sheet gets" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **One new row** with the answers of the test order.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Ten customers send the order form. What does the sheet show?

   - [x] ten rows, one for each response

     Why: Each response is one row of the sheet.

   - [ ] one row with all the orders

     Why: Every response gets its own row.

   - [ ] nothing: Mona must type the orders

     Why: The form fills the sheet by itself.
   :::
